name: gameplay-cinema-ride
origin: A ride on the gameplay screen (checkpoint 4, slice c; extended in checkpoint 5): the round of gameplay-cinema-bomb (AI robots stopped at its first frame); the pickup fixture gives the player a CarProp on its cell, collected on the next engine frame (mount: CarProp.changeStage, resetRobotMc: _r0_Car_Down at frame 1), the player drives down (drive: the clip playing) and releases the key after 10 frames (release: one frame on, the clip has advanced once more, as the player advances a playing clip's timeline before the frame's scripts run moveStop; parked: two frames later, at frame 715, standing on that frame).
godot_note: Godot starts on the recorded round (round cinema-start) as gameplay-cinema-start does, and stops its AI robots with the Godot-only ai-stop action.

wall_clock_text./@0#1/@0/time: Game.countTime counts Date seconds; the reference player's Date follows the host clock, not its stepped frames, so TIME reads 178 or 177 here depending on the machine

actions.godot_note: The app does not reproduce the menus' Math.random draws, so the round this START opens replays the original's generator from the recording (math_random.json) and rolls its board from the original's draws (Layouts.roll_set: it must equal the golden's boxes and frames); the enemy robots come from the golden of the cinema-start capture (App.round_as_recorded).
AIControl.stop through the original's own method (fixture); Godot gives the robot no commands, as it then has none.

The pickup fixture makes the original's own pickup class on the player's cell (AbstractItem.init), collected by GetItemCommand on the next engine frame; Godot puts the same pickup on the player's cell (Game.give_pickup).
